text: Split-conformal validity rests on exchangeability, which fails when observations come in groups drawn from distinct distributions (e.g. several observations per unit), as with many fields or slots per PDF document.
quote: The validity of conformal prediction hinges on the exchangeability of the data, which does not hold when groups of observations come from distinct distributions, such as multiple observations on each patient in a medical database.

text: With hierarchically structured data (groups, repeated measurements) standard exchangeability may not hold; a hierarchical form of exchangeability is needed to extend conformal methods.
quote: for example, groups of observations, or repeated measurements. In such settings, standard notions of exchangeability may not hold. To address this challenge, a hierarchical form of exchangeability is derived

text: Learn-then-Test assumes the calibration set is i.i.d.; slots that cluster within documents violate this unless the document is the sampling unit.
quote: be the calibration set, an independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) set of variables, where the feature vectors Xi take values in X

text: Learn-then-Test reframes risk control as multiple hypothesis testing over candidate thresholds, giving high-probability (PAC-style) rather than in-expectation control.
quote: Our main insight is to reframe the risk-control problem as multiple hypothesis testing, enabling techniques and mathematical arguments different from those in the previous literature.

text: Conformal risk control guarantees risk only in expectation over calibration draws, unlike high-probability risk-control methods; a single calibrated threshold can exceed the budget.
quote: the algorithm presented herein differs greatly: it has a guarantee in expectation, and neither the algorithm nor its analysis share much technical similarity with these previous works.

text: zlib-bitexact-rs's public raw-DEFLATE API is pinned to level 9 and memLevel 8 (zlib 1.3.1 parameters); replaying other levels or memLevels needs a patch or fork, as done in OBS-1100.
quote: byte-identical to stock zlib 1.3.1 with `deflateInit2(9, Z_DEFLATED, -15, 8,

text: On document extraction, fields cluster within documents: the measured design effect is 1.84 to 2.45 across three corpora, roughly halving the effective calibration sample.
quote: At the add-one threshold the estimated design effect is 2.15 (CORD), 1.84 (FUNSD), 2.04 (XFUND-de) — up to 2.45 at other thresholds — so the effective calibration sample is roughly half its nominal size.

text: Per-group binomial (Mondrian LTT) certificates assume iid errors within a group; with a design effect of about 2 the binomial n overstates the evidence about twofold, so a cluster-corrected variant must be co-reported.
quote: The iid premise is load-bearing, not decorative: the measured design effect ≈2 means the binomial n overstates evidence about twofold; we therefore co-report a cluster-corrected variant

text: A certificate that treats the document as the iid unit is valid but near-vacuous at this scale (0.060 coverage, 47.5% of splits certify nothing).
quote: The doc-iid tier is honest but near-vacuous (0.060 coverage, 47.5% zero-coverage splits). Powered document-level PAC procedures are the named open problem.

text: Powered document-level risk-control procedures (clustered or variance-adaptive bounds) are named as an open problem at 800 documents.
quote: This is the honest price of document-level exchangeability at 800 documents; powered doc-level procedures (clustered/variance-adaptive bounds)

text: Marginal guarantees do not imply per-group guarantees: under mild group-composition shift, standard conformal risk control violated the risk budget in up to 47% of evaluation trials.
quote: under mild distributional shift in group composition, standard CRC violates the risk budget in up to 47% of evaluation trials.

text: HG-CRC enforces simultaneous risk guarantees across every node of a user-defined group hierarchy (Bonferroni over nodes, leaf-first threshold selection with fallback to coarser nodes).
quote: a posthoc calibration framework that enforces simultaneous risk guarantees across all nodes of a user-defined group hierarchy. HG-CRC applies a Bonferroni correction over hierarchy nodes and uses a leaf-first selection policy

text: In a web-PDF corpus, the 1 MiB crawl cap truncated 23.06% of documents but these held 63.08% of the text: document counts badly understate truncation's text impact.
quote: at the 1 MiB cap in force at the time, corresponding to 23.06% of them. Those documents hold 63.08% of the corpus's text (Table 2).

text: Truncated fragments were reconstructed by cutting the untruncated originals at 1 MiB and extracting text from both fragment and whole file; recoverability may be a property of the parser rather than of the file.
quote: truncated documents at 1 MiB, and extract text from both the fragment and the whole file. Whether a fragment is recoverable may be a property of the parser rather than of the file

text: On the same truncated fragments PyMuPDF recovers 11.4% of tokens and 20.7% of pages, PDFium 1.4% and 1.9%: an 8.4x engine gap on identical input.
quote: PyMuPDF recovers 11.4% of the tokens and 20.7% of the pages; PDFium recovers 1.4% and 1.9%, a gap of 8.4× on identical input.

text: A truncated file that opens can still be empty: MuPDF rebuilds a missing xref, reports a page count, and returns no text for 72.4% of truncated files (a plausible-but-wrong success).
quote: the page content streams lie beyond the cut, so the document opens, reports a page count, and returns no text: 72.4% yield nothing at all.

text: Linearized PDFs recover less after truncation, not more: under PyMuPDF 1.1% of tokens versus 18.5% for non-linearized files (PDFium 1.1% versus 1.5%).
quote: Under PyMuPDF those files recover 1.1% of their tokens against 18.5% for the non-linearized rest, while under PDFium it is 1.1% against 1.5%.
